I've been running XBMCbuntu for years with a pretty complex streaming setup, even going as far as grabbing the Netflix stream from a virtualized PlayOn server running out of my ESXi lab downstairs, and I've had no problems. After the project swapped over to KODI, I went with whatever the carryover is -- I think it's KODIbuntu, but I don't have the system handy at the moment to check. This is an old first-gen Atom processor with practically no ram, and it streams everything from a local fileserver via wifi; the only thing it has going for it is an SSD, which ensures near instant boot times, and that's how I get around having to deal with any sort of suspend/hibernate issues... I just turn it off, but the BIOS is keyed to power on from the keyboard, and those old USB IR sensors with a Microsoft HTPC remote are set to keyboard keys, and... well, you get where I'm going; easy on/off and quick power up/down.

As far as video codecs go, man... I've got everything on that server from stuff that was encoded back in the 90s to stuff that I crunch down in handbrake last week, and KODI plays all of it without a problem.

I do have an SSD in the machine too. The bios is keyed to wake from USB (Edit, I basically just mash the keyboard which we leave on top of the fridge and the computer resumes, then I can turn on the TV and control everything from my smartphone, its on the fridge so the kids can't get to it). That was my biggest concern, easy on/off and sleep/suspend. I have been swayed to at least try it out, this weekend will be a fun adventure.

Should be noted also that KODI has a "remote app" in the Google Play store that works well. It's wifi, and you just mark a checkbox in KODI's advanced options to enable the remote, then point the app at your HTPC's ip address, and presto... instant remote.

So, I've cut the cord long ago, and live in a Windows free house. Kodi.tv/XBMC and Plex are perfectly capable of handling your videos and stuff.

The tough part comes with the dual monitors playing two different things. Typically, this isn't how Media Center PCs are designed to operate. Usually you have one head-end dediated to playing one particular thing. Not to say it can't be done, I've just never tried, and doing something a bit different can sometimes require quite a bit more knowledge than expected.

With that said, I've seen plex, and it can do mostly everything that Kodi can do.... however you will sacrifice some customizability in favor of being more user friendly. Plex is very very easy to set up, and is damn near a push button HTPC solution. Kodi is arguably slightly more difficult to set up, but does require a lot of researching for the more complex configurations. However, the community is very strong, and generally helpful.

Back in the day, DRM was an issue with streaming, but mostly, that's been resolved. That's not to say you won't encounter a bump here and there... These issues could also be resolved by now, its been about a year since I've had netflix, amazon prime, or other streaming services (I use a local file server).

If you're interested or care in such things, Kodi is completely open source. Plex is not. Not that I'm going to judge anyone that runs Plex, just saying...

If you ever get stuck with any of the linux part, feel free to hit me up directly via PM. I've hit a lot of walls in the past and might be able to at least push you in the right direction.

A linux based HTPC opens up so many more possibilities than Windows can ever possibly compete with, so If you're willing to weather a few bumps here and there to get your 'dream setup', you'll not regret it one bit.
